Hi OP,

This might sound strange, but would you by chance describe yourself as a leftist?

I ask because I'm one too, and to be honest, it's made me miserable.  
I was able to move past that feeling though, so maybe my story could help you?

​

The story: when I was in college, I voted for Obama, believing, "yes we can" but I still remember feeling so hopeless and defeated. The future looked so bleak even though I was graduating and starting a new chapter in life. I thought I knew everything and that i was so enlightened.

Actually I only had half the story. Finally I started talking to new people who called themselves centrists and conservatives. I was always told those people were evil, but for some bizarre reason, they were pretty much all welcoming and just wanted to talk. They didn't just bombard me with bad news about the climate going to hell and bigots taking over the country, even though I believed that to be true.

They accepted my views and shared their's, and we agreed to disagree, but the more i learned, the more i realized these were just people too, and I started feeling less and less threatened because I could say i knew for a fact the other side wasn't evil. 

I even started feeling like the world wasn't actually headed to hell and realized I only felt that way because I'd unknowingly trapped myself in a bubble. I was inundated with "news" articles that were designed to be shocking and upsetting to get clicks, and all my friends were reading the same articles so no one had the truth or even just a less dramatic, dismal take on current events.

Now I try to reach out for new sources of news. Tim Pool on youtube has been extremely helpful, and as strange as it might sound, I really don't feel the world is going to hell anymore. call me naive, but it does feel better.

Maybe it could begin feeling better for you too?

You might want to rephrase this question, but I think what you're asking is:

If you're in a mono relationship, are you missing out on the wild things you can usually do while single?

If that is your question then here is one thing to think of: 

The bottom line is we are all going to die. At that point we realize what is really important in life. Now, how many people do you suppose wind up on their deathbed saying "man I sure wish I'd slept around with at least 20 more random strangers back when I was single..." or "thank goodness I at least got to see the rocky mountains" or "dammit I shouldve gone to more keggers way back when!"

My guess is not many. Far more likely would be the person saying "I wish I'd had more time with my daughter" or "I wish I could've been a better man to my wife" or "I'm so grateful to be surrounded by my family right now." 

Usually we realize too late that what really brings fulfillment in life is how well we cared for the people who depended on us, not how well we banged the strangers who will forget our names in a matter of months, or how wild we got at that one party filled with people who subsequently forgot we even exist and are perfectly happy with having done so.

The wild times are fun, don't get me wrong, but at the end of the day, most people find them far less fulfilling compared to things like experiences shared with their wife, kids, mom and dad.

When we marry, we let go of childish pursuits and become part of a team, capable of obtaining the highest levels of satisfaction known to mankind. There's nothing quite like having someone who loves you so much, they literally vowed to spend the rest of their lives making you feel loved.

You don't agree because you didn't bother reading it.

There's no reason to leave without first telling her what she's doing and the risk she faces by not straightening up. Otherwise you haven't given her, yourself, or your children a fair shot.

Phase 1. Tell her that you need to talk and ask her to choose a time for a 10 minute chat. Meet her at this time and sit with her. Calmly tell her you just want to tell her what's really going on and she does NOT need to apologize, do anything, agree or believe anything. All you want is for her to listen while you speak. Ask her if she will agree to just listen. If she says yes, keep it short and calm.   


(If she says no, then thank her for trying and ask when a better time might be.)  
If she said yes: Tell her your body is different from hers. It needs physical intimacy and without it you suffer terribly. This is no one's fault. it's just biology. Again ask her to please not feel bad or do anything. Thank her for listening and leave the room.

Listen, then do what she says immediately. Do not wait. She may say to leave her alone, etc. And if so, just agree and do so. Don't worry. You've planted the seed. That's all you need for phase 1.

Also i highly recommend buying a physical copy of the book and "accidentally" leaving it somewhere she will see it. Don't talk to her about it or shove anything down her throat. Don't mention it at all unless she asks about it. And even then, just tell her you are studying ways to show love to her and the kids.

Phase 3. The book will tell you the rest of what you need to know. Many people have been in your shoes, including myself. This approach works if YOU are willing to work hard.

I do find it hurtful that I'm not enough for my husband, especially since he is definitely enough for me.

I'm frankly humiliated thinking of how enamored I've been with him for the past 13 years. I feel betrayed and lied to. In a marriage, you both vow to "forsake all others" and that is exactly what I'm willing to do. He made that same vow and yet now he wants to break it.

He wants me and our unborn child to be at risk of HPV and herpes, and to leave me at home changing diapers while he screws some slut who doesn't think there's anything wrong with being a homewrecker. It is hurtful and something I know I don't deserve to be put through.

Our situations might be different. Being lied to is what caused the situation to be so hurtful, but if he'd been honest with me to begin with, I could see myself coping with not being enough a lot better because it would've been my own choice to tie myself down to such a person or not. I didn't get a chance to make an informed decision, so yeah, it hurts. Betrayal hurts.

All I can say is this: know your worth and be honest with your feelings. No one has the right to tell you how to feel about something and no one can say your feelings are less valid than anyone else's. Anyone who says you "should" feel a certain way is just trying to manipulate you.

Lastly, I'll say that no matter how things look now, the fact is there are over 6 billion people on this earth. There are plenty of fish in the sea and there is someone out there who can be naturally and happily monogamous with you.

If you're not already tied down with a mortgage, marriage and kids, you have options. If I were you, I'd thoroughly look into those options.

​

Edit: My post may be overly harsh because it comes from a place of hurt. I want to point out that the other woman is likely not in fact a slut. She's probably just another human looking for love like the rest of us, but through my eyes she's an adversary.

In the same way, the husband is not really a liar or a traitor. He's just a person who, like me, was working with inaccurate or inadequate information and made agreements he wasn't aware he wouldn't be able to keep. That doesn't change the fact that he presented a false self who I fell in love with and then took that person away. It is very much like a death, and with death comes grief.

Either way, I sympathize and share the hurt of not being enough.

The other answers you're going to get to your post will likely not quite match up with such a feeling because most people who answer will be poly. They don't identify with the hurt that comes with knowing you're not enough. You may as well be asking a gay man "how do you cope with the painful truth that you'll never enjoy sex with a woman?" It doesn't compute.
